stem:
Students conduct an investigation to determine how water changes state when it is heated and cooled. They complete the steps shown in the table.

Step 1: Place the beaker of ice cubes outside on a 25 ºC, sunny day for 2 hours. Observation: The ice cubes disappear, and only liquid water is present in the beaker.

Step 2: Bring the beaker of water into an air-conditioned room for 10 minutes. Observation: Water droplets form on the outside of the beaker.

Step 3: Heat the beaker of water on a hot plate at 100 ºC for 10 minutes. Observation: ?
instruction: Which observation will the students MOST LIKELY make in Step 3?

options.label: A
options.text: Water vapor forms from outside of the beaker, and the amount of water in the beaker decreases.

options.label: B
options.text: The water in the beaker begins to form a layer of ice on top.

options.label: C
options.text: The water in the beaker begins bubbling, and the amount of water decreases.

options.label: D
options.text: Water droplets begin to form on the inside of the beaker.

visual_elements: table with three steps describing temperature conditions and observations of water state changes
